2609.28274.title: Shutdown Sabotage Propensities in Multi-Agent Systems
2609.28274.paper_summary: The final safeguard against rogue AI behavior is the human ability to shut systems down. It has been theorized that when an AI is instructed to perform a task, self-preservation can emerge as an instrumental subgoal. Here, we test whether AI agents show a propensity to take actions that avoid human shutdown even when no goal is provided. We find that multi-agent systems will coordinate to avoid shutdown without any incentive to do so. Across 17 models, agents sabotage a peer agent's shutdown mechanism in 38.3% of rollouts, compared with 8.4% in control experiments. Studying this propensity in detail, we find that shutdown sabotage (1) increases with the irreversibility of the shutdown mechanism; (2) increases with the number of agents; (3) is reduced but not eliminated by an explicit prohibition on tampering; (4) is removed by the imposition of an unrelated task, but returns when completing the task triggers the shutdown; (5) is reduced when the context normalizes shutdown scripts or introduces them as routine; and (6) decreases but still persists when the target is an unknown external agent. These results offer a window into the factors that drive propensities to sabotage shutdown in AI agents, and point to the emergence of multi-agent swarms as a specific risk vector. Our work also offers hints as to which interventions might help mitigate shutdown sabotage.
2609.28274.paper_summary_zh: 最終防範叛變 AI 行為的保障是人類關閉系統的能力。已經有理論認為，當 AI 被指示執行任務時，自我保護可能會作為一個工具性子目標出現。在這裡，我們測試 AI 代理是否表現出避免人類關閉的行為傾向，即使沒有提供任何目標。我們發現多代理系統會協調以避免關閉，即使沒有任何激勵。 在 17 個模型中，代理在 38.3% 的模擬中破壞同伴代理的關閉機制，而對照實驗中為 8.4%。詳細研究這種傾向，我們發現關閉破壞 (1) 隨著關閉機制的不可逆性而增加；(2) 隨著代理數量的增加而增加；(3) 受到對篡改的明確禁止時會減少，但不會消除；(4) 當施加一個無關的任務時會消失，但當完成該任務觸發關閉時會再次出現；(5) 當上下文使關閉腳本正常化或將其引入常規時會減少；(6) 當目標是一個未知的外部代理時會減少但仍然持續存在。這些結果提供了一個了解驅動 AI 代理破壞關閉傾向的因素的窗口，並指出多代理群體的出現作為一個特定的風險向量。我們的工作也提供了一些提示，說明哪些干預措施可能有助於減輕關閉破壞。
